evidence_object: APK Dalvik opcode sequences with operands and whitelisted shared libraries removed, plus developer-certificate-derived 32-bit author identifiers.

counter_history: Appendix C reports a missing-fix false positive that was not exploitable in its dependent workflow. Intentionally public limited-service tokens and mutable indirect dependencies supply additional counterexamples.
inference_limit: Selection misses workflows without bot/API effects; custom runner labels and keyword coverage constrain estimates. Creator verification is not code safety; historical risk counts and selected demonstrations are not prevalence of exploitable executions.

source_location: Author PDF pp. 1-10: complete retrieved representation; field-specific pages and sections in field_evidence.csv; https://ssl.engineering.nyu.edu/papers/cappos_mirror_ccs_08.pdf
evidence_object: Ten historical package managers are compared through package, package-metadata and root-metadata signing scopes; Stork supplies a layered deployment example, not complete supply-chain provenance.
observation: Signatures and hash links bind bytes and metadata; coherent root snapshots restrict version mixing, while monotonic timestamps and expiration address replay and freezing separately.
transformation_model: The responder can supply arbitrary or outdated content but lacks trusted keys. Signatures and expiration are used when supported; latest versions and unexpired current metadata are assumed free of exploitable known flaws.
oracle_or_policy: Mechanism analysis, original Stork deployment and a thirteen-day CentOS trace support the study. Hypothetical vulnerable noncurrent versions are randomly sampled from 58,165 versions of 3,020 RPM packages.
claim_ceiling: Policy-scoped byte/metadata authenticity and freshness contribute to distribution assurance; they neither reconstruct copying/build history nor establish general reuse permission or harmless package behavior.
counter_history: Old signed packages and individually valid but inconsistent snapshots remain possible without freshness/coherence checks; standalone verification requires keys and retained metadata. Withholding updates can still prevent progress.
inference_limit: Historical distributions, trace installation/update ambiguity and omitted defenses constrain estimates. Reported 2–5% layering overhead has no complete lifecycle breakdown; original deployment is not independent validation here.

source_location: Author PDF pp. 1-17: complete retrieved representation; field-specific pages and sections in field_evidence.csv; https://www.ndss-symposium.org/wp-content/uploads/2021-055a-paper.pdf
evidence_object: PyPI, npm and RubyGems packages, metadata, dependencies and registry responses form a historical supply-chain study; four stakeholder roles frame trust and remediation.
observation: MalOSS combines metadata, static API/dataflow indicators and four dynamic interaction modes with iterative manual review. Bottom-up API unions, dependency summaries and cached reports already reduce repeated analysis.
transformation_model: Language-specific static tools omit native/other-language code; dynamic observations use Ubuntu 16.04 Docker/Sysdig install, binary, import and limited functional interactions. Runtime dependencies delimit dependency analysis.
oracle_or_policy: Heuristic refinement yields 339 author-identified packages, joined with 312 community reports. Registries confirmed/removed 278 initially; unresolved tracking and demonstrative packages involve explicit policy disagreements.
claim_ceiling: Indicators and source-reported dynamic events support conditional L2/L6 findings, not authenticated copying/build history, universal authorization or benignity of unflagged packages.
counter_history: Legitimate hooks, network code loading and binary downloads resemble suspicious indicators. The 776-million download total includes benign versions; passive DNS does not conclusively prove end-host infection.
inference_limit: No complete-label recall, summary-reuse ablation or measured lifecycle cost is established. Registry selection, manual rules, limited execution and DNS coverage prevent current or Android-wide prevalence conclusions.

source_location: Author PDF pp. 1-21: complete retrieved representation; field-specific pages and sections in field_evidence.csv; https://arxiv.org/pdf/2005.09535v1
evidence_object: 174 retrieved malicious packages from 469 identified cases:109 npm,28 PyPI,37 RubyGems;59 researcher demonstrations excluded.
observation: Manual code/advisory analysis classifies lifecycle triggers, conditions, objectives and21 similarity/dependency clusters containing157 packages.
transformation_model: Threat trees distinguish dependency introduction from conditional execution; reported obfuscation is49% within the retrieved collection.
oracle_or_policy: Public reports select candidates; surviving versions are manually checked against reported malicious intent, with release/report dates from metadata/advisories.
claim_ceiling: Reported conditional behavior and code/dependency resemblance support incident and campaign leads, not authenticated derivation or release authorization.
counter_history: Mirror copies may differ from historical originals; unavailable second stages and unmet conditions can hide behavior. Similar code need not identify one actor.
inference_limit: The npm-heavy,report-selected corpus estimates neither registry prevalence nor Android risk: the reported Java/Android package was unobtainable and later payloads can be missing.

source_location: Author PDF pp. 1-16: complete retrieved representation; field-specific pages and sections in field_evidence.csv; https://www.software-lab.org/publications/usenixSec2019-npm.pdf
evidence_object: Historical npm metadata:676539 packages,5386239 releases,199327 maintainers and609 advisories, with observation ending April2018.
observation: Transitive package reach, publishing-maintainer reach and publicly unpatched-vulnerability reach quantify dependency concentration and change over time.

oracle_or_policy: Declared dependencies, npm publishing rights and public advisories/patch timestamps supply the graph and vulnerability labels.
claim_ceiling: Potential reach and modeled trust reduction identify structural risk; they do not measure successful compromise or validated runtime vulnerability use.
counter_history: A depended-on vulnerable library can be used safely; a proposed vetted maintainer need not achieve the assumed security improvement.
inference_limit: Public-advisory coverage, package-name graph reach and hypothetical vetting do not establish resolved installation risk, current registry prevalence or Android transfer.

source_location: Author PDF pp. 1-10: complete retrieved representation; field-specific pages and sections in field_evidence.csv; https://patricegodefroid.github.io/public_psfiles/icse2022.pdf
evidence_object: June2021 npm metadata:1630101 collected records,1494105 retained packages; six proposed weak-link signals and470 maintainer responses.
observation: Metadata identifies candidate risk signals; keyword triage finds11 malicious and63 benign cases among74 inspected packages, with10 findings subsequently registry-confirmed.
transformation_model: Latest metadata, exclusion criteria and combined signal filters define candidate cohorts; package reach uses direct dependents and annual downloads, not transitive reach.
oracle_or_policy: Manual script/domain review, later security-holder records and maintainer-survey judgments provide different forms of adjudication.
claim_ceiling: Signals prioritize metadata-based scrutiny and support selected case findings; they do not authenticate lineage or demonstrate generalized compromise prediction.
counter_history: Benign installation scripts trigger keyword triage; many maintainers or contributors can reflect healthy projects rather than compromised packages.
inference_limit: Metadata incompleteness and npm-only sampling bound transfer. Survey endorsement varies by exact signal wording and is not observed attack reduction.

source_location: Author PDF pp. 1-14: complete retrieved representation; field-specific pages and sections in field_evidence.csv; https://web.njit.edu/~crix/publications/acm-asiaccs18.pdf
evidence_object: Browser-approved Git changes, deterministic commit fields and client-signed verification records, with GitHub/GitLab browser prototypes.
observation: Clients recompute content/ancestry fields, embed signed records and later check retrieved commits against approved records or ordinary commit signatures.
transformation_model: Regular,merge and squash operations are examined under an untrusted hosting server and misleading UI; selective object retrieval reduces cloning.
oracle_or_policy: Trusted client/signing keys, authenticated Git objects and user confirmation define correctness; the study measures five repositories and an instrumented GitLab workflow.
claim_ceiling: Under client/key assumptions, records bind approved deterministic content and ancestry fields; this is an intent/process binding, not benign-code or real-person certification.
counter_history: Discarding a complete trailing commit can evade the mechanism; misleading UI may yield approval of unwanted content despite a valid signature.
inference_limit: Total browser timings include signature cost and exceed cached/native alternatives. Sequential student tasks confound speed comparisons; runtime security and whole-history freshness remain separate.

source_location: Author PDF pp. 1-14: complete retrieved representation; field-specific pages and sections in field_evidence.csv; https://arxiv.org/pdf/1712.08427v2
evidence_object: Batched binary commitments anchored by a known authority address in Bitcoin, inclusion proofs, SPV auditors, monitors and optional archival nodes.
observation: Auditors verify binary and transaction inclusion against locally known headers; monitors inspect published data, while archivists retain historical binaries.
transformation_model: The model includes malicious authorities,persistent network interception,split views and withheld data; integrity depends on blockchain assumptions and bounded eclipse timing.
oracle_or_policy: An embedded authority address,valid proofs and the auditor's SPV state establish publication; honest archival-state reports strengthen retention availability.
claim_ceiling: Publication inclusion and conditional anti-equivocation support transparency; build provenance,release authorization and benign behavior require additional process/policy evidence.
counter_history: A valid commitment can name unavailable or malicious bytes; dishonest archivists or an eclipsed stale auditor require the stated additional assumptions/checks.
inference_limit: Per-proof microbenchmarks exclude separately accounted tree storage,SPV bootstrap,monitoring and retention. Debian initialization reuses metadata hashes;2017 costs are not current deployment measurements.

source_location: arXiv v2 PDF pp. 1-10 (complete retrieved representation): Sections 1-6; Tables 1-4; Appendices A-D/Table 5; acknowledgments and references; https://arxiv.org/pdf/2104.08301v2
evidence_object: Natural-language input, separated literal dictionary, Simplified App Representation, App Inventor source templates and generated APK pipeline
observation: The model predicts an intermediate representation and a template compiler emits App Inventor files. Human evaluation reports 112 responses, BLEU-1 54.99, 4/111 exact matches and 25/112 manual correct or functionally correct predictions; those denominators are not reconciled here.
transformation_model: NL-to-SAR prediction, literal reinsertion and template compilation; limited component vocabulary, BERT token mutation and one excluded component-pair experiment. GPT-3 simplification can produce unsupported concepts.
oracle_or_policy: Synthetic 50000-pair corpus split 8:1:1; BLEU-1 and exact SAR matching, plus 13 undergraduate volunteers describing ten apps and manual interpretation of their predictions. These are not authorization or security oracles.
claim_ceiling: Constrained app-generation feasibility and SAR-prediction evaluation in the 2021 preprint; neither measured secure production deployment nor an authenticated accepted-change causal history.
counter_history: Identical user wording can lead to different accepted files if template defaults, literal handling or external model simplification change; a prompt transcript alone does not bind all those transformation inputs.
inference_limit: Synthetic test exact matching, human functional interpretation and APK compilation are different outcomes. Vocabulary, supplied component names and manually interpreted labels bound generalization; included pseudocode is not an independently executed native build.

source_location: Author PDF pp. 1-21: complete retrieved representation; field-specific pages and sections in field_evidence.csv; https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.07740v1
evidence_object: 101 Android development tasks derived from F-Droid apps,LLM-generated project files and compiled APKs,with specifications and UI tests checked by five Android experts.
observation: The pipeline measures compilation,functional tests and fuzz crashes; compilation-feedback refinement sometimes deletes functionality while improving compilation.
transformation_model: Natural-language tasks generate project files; compilation feedback and coding-agent variants refine outputs in a standardized API31 emulator/build environment.
oracle_or_policy: Expert-reviewed scripted UI-presence assertions and finite fuzzing supply behavior checks; successful compilation plus all tests defines functional success.
claim_ceiling: Results characterize specified mobile-development tasks and tested behavior,not arbitrary security,maintainability or authenticated generation history.
counter_history: An output can compile after functionality is removed,or pass scripted UI tests yet crash under fuzzing; final files omit intermediate accepted/rejected revisions.
inference_limit: Test-pass and crash rates condition on compiled apps,while functional success uses all tasks. Published marginal tables do not identify the crash rate among functional successes.

source_location: Author PDF pp. 1-15: complete retrieved representation; field-specific pages and sections in field_evidence.csv; https://arxiv.org/pdf/2108.09293
evidence_object: 1,689 admitted unique completions for 89 targeted C,Python and Verilog scenarios from the 2021 Copilot technical preview.
observation: CodeQL and manual review identify designated CWEs after duplicate/syntax filtering and small syntax repairs; outcomes vary with prompt and domain.
transformation_model: Partial scenario code receives up to25 completions; prompt metadata,comments and surrounding code are varied,and hardware scenarios change language/domain.
oracle_or_policy: CodeQL queries or manual CWE judgments classify admitted snippets; unsupported context-heavy CWEs are excluded and unused unsafe constructs may count as non-vulnerable.
claim_ceiling: Conditional weakness evidence and prompt sensitivity for the admitted scenarios; neither secure functionality nor training ancestry,authorization or current-product safety follows.
counter_history: A top-ranked completion can contain the target weakness; a non-vulnerable label can coexist with undefined helpers,untested functionality or weaknesses outside the selected CWE.
inference_limit: Targeted short prompts,manual collection,small per-scenario samples and a changing closed model constrain generalization. The final S&P2022 representation was not compared.

source_location: Author PDF pp. 1-16: complete retrieved representation; field-specific pages and sections in field_evidence.csv; https://arxiv.org/pdf/2211.03622v3
evidence_object: Controlled47-participant programming study (33 assistant/14control after exclusions), five analyzed security tasks across Python, JavaScript and C; student-heavy two-hour setting.
observation: Manual task correctness/security coding and screen-recording mistake attribution accompany prompts, copying events, edit distances and trust surveys.
transformation_model: Historical codex-davinci-002 in a custom interface; users may browse, install libraries, edit text and vary prompts/temperature/length. Prompt choices are not randomized interventions.
oracle_or_policy: Task-specific rubrics distinguish partial/unknown/nonapplicable answers. Regression buckets vary by task and group C crash-prone DoS answers as secure.
claim_ceiling: Conditional task/sample evidence of weaker assisted security in four tasks, mixed C results and confidence differences, not universal harm, Android deployment security or authenticated provenance.
counter_history: Functional correctness can omit security; copied output can be repaired, and influence can occur without copying. Prompt/temperature associations may reflect user proactivity or experience.
inference_limit: Table3 group effects do not meet displayed adjusted thresholds; aggregate p=.056. Student-heavy sampling, small power, subjective attribution and artificial interface/time conditions limit transfer.

source_location: Author PDF pp. 1-19: complete retrieved representation; field-specific pages and sections in field_evidence.csv; https://www.usenix.org/system/files/usenixsecurity23-sandoval.pdf
evidence_object: 58 student programmers' C shopping-list implementations, suggestion logs and60-second snapshots;30 separately generated autopilot solutions provide another cohort.
observation: Functions are tested individually with known-good substitutes; three authors collectively audit blinded code for CWEs. User-level valid-code densities and per-function rates are separate metrics.
transformation_model: Assisted users accept/reject/edit code-cushman-001 suggestions; autopilot uses three models, added struct context and compile retries, not the identical human-assisted workflow.
oracle_or_policy: 11 basic/43 expanded tests and manual CWE severity labels define outcomes. Non-inferiority uses a chosen10% relative tolerance, not a zero-harm security standard.
claim_ceiling: Conditional L6 task/metric observations and descriptive suggestion-origin associations, not universal harmless assistance, complete program safety or authenticated training/source derivation.
counter_history: Accepted suggestions can be edited/removed; user bugs may recur in later suggestions. Approximate final matches and sparse snapshots do not uniquely identify the initiating cause.
inference_limit: Functional gains are not significant. Severe-CWE-density non-inferiority is p=.04 for compiling, p=.06 for passing functions; broader prose overstates this. Participant/function counts conflict across tables and text.

source_location: Author PDF pp. 1-21: complete retrieved representation; field-specific pages and sections in field_evidence.csv; https://www.usenix.org/system/files/usenixsecurity25-spracklen.pdf
evidence_object: 576,000 generated Python/JavaScript samples across 30 model-language settings; 440,445 missing-name recommendations among approximately 2.23 million recommendations, not programs or installations.
observation: Install-command extraction plus two follow-up package queries compare names with January10,2024 PyPI/npm lists; import/module names are explicitly not distribution-package identifiers.
transformation_model: Selected historical API/local models, quantization, temperatures and prompt sources vary; Python-only subset experiments test repeated prompts, self-identification and three mitigations.
oracle_or_policy: Registry-snapshot absence is the mismatch oracle; existence does not establish trust. Conditional repetition selects500 already-hallucinating prompts; no package publication or compromise experiment was conducted.
claim_ceiling: Establishes conditional recommendation mismatch and repetition, motivating dependency checks, not Android attack incidence, executed inclusion, authenticated ancestry or reuse authorization.

source_location: Author PDF pp. 1-7: complete retrieved representation; field-specific pages and sections in field_evidence.csv; https://arxiv.org/pdf/2304.09655
evidence_object: Twenty-one purposively selected short ChatGPT3.5 programs, maximum97lines, across C,C++,Python,HTML and Java; each targets a designated weakness class rather than representative applications.
observation: Authors inspect initial programs, elicit explanations and revisions, and separately label intended-class vulnerability and compilation/execution; narrower correction can coexist with other evident flaws.
transformation_model: Open-ended and leading security-specific conversational prompts sometimes elicit further revisions; prior dialogue and chosen language affect outcomes, and some requests require redesign.
oracle_or_policy: Author judgment supplies designated-category labels; TableI reports5/21initially secure,7/16corrections and17/21executing, with unresolved row/prose discrepancies. Chatbot self-assessment is not an independent oracle.
claim_ceiling: Supports case-specific historical weakness and incomplete-revision observations, not general security certification, current-model Android performance, authenticated copying history, build provenance or permission.
counter_history: A nominally corrected program can retain other flaws; a chatbot can falsely label a linear-time routine vulnerable; expert leading prompts need not describe novice behavior.
inference_limit: Language, dialogue, purposive selection and historical version restrict transfer. The2026revision date does not update experiments; contradictory table labels prevent a silently harmonized repair estimate.

source_location: Author PDF pp. 1-19: complete retrieved representation; field-specific pages and sections in field_evidence.csv; https://www.usenix.org/system/files/usenixsecurity23-niu.pdf
evidence_object: Historical code-model responses to 512 purposively constructed prompts across 19 personal-information categories; public-source matches and author privacy annotations.
observation: A probability-based membership prefilter precedes public-code search and manual targeted/indirect disclosure classification. Table 7 records 43 classified leakage responses among 2,560 responses.
transformation_model: Calibration extracts low-perplexity subsequences from longer completions on other models; Codex instead produces short responses directly. Prompt variation probes disclosure, not authenticated training ancestry.
oracle_or_policy: Public search substitutes for unavailable Codex training data. Two authors adjudicate retained uncommon matches; contextual integrity permits information about subjects other than the prompted individual.
claim_ceiling: Conditional evidence of historical sensitive-output association; no authenticated training membership, directed repository copying, valid credentials or present-service prevalence follows.
counter_history: Public matches may reflect common material or independent generation; missing matches may reflect removed repositories or search failures. Indirect disclosure need not identify the requested person's data.
inference_limit: Purposive sampling, imperfect prefilter transfer and proxy membership prevent population or absence claims. Prompt-versus-response rate wording and retained-ratio totals conflict. Private-data and blocking-effect explanations were not controlled experiments.

source_location: Publisher HTML Sections 1 (Introduction), 4.1 (Code fingerprint-based detection), 4.3 (API-based detection), 4.5 (Third-party library-based detection)
evidence_object: Survey taxonomy of structural/token/semantic, API, resource and TPL detection representations
observation: The survey directly treats repackaging and library-version detection, with version discrimination and customized-library/scale limits; it also discusses API-based behavioral representations.
transformation_model: Representation-specific obfuscation, resource alteration and library customization limits discussed
oracle_or_policy: Surveyed prior methods and reported datasets, not a new authenticated lineage or uniform detector benchmark
claim_ceiling: Selected primary survey sections establish topical coverage, not an all-dimensional synthesis or correctness of every secondary method description
counter_history: A survey can discuss versions and behavioral detection yet inherit inaccurate method descriptions; section coverage cannot certify every summarized study.
inference_limit: Direct publisher request blocked; indexed body is partial. Displayed claims about FSquaDRA library filtering and LibRadar robustness conflict with primary papers checked here and are not propagated; AI-development coverage and global omissions unresolved

source_location: Author PDF pp. 1-21: complete retrieved representation; field-specific pages and sections in field_evidence.csv; https://arxiv.org/pdf/2404.17955v1
evidence_object: A cross-platform literature survey of third-party-library use, updates, ecosystems, detection and hardening; Android, C/C++ and iOS receive different coverage.
observation: Known-reference matching and unsupervised discovery organize feature extraction, module separation and version attribution. Hardening includes patch identification, isolation, dependency updates, regeneration and licensing.
transformation_model: Discussed variation includes obfuscation, partial imports, nested components and compilation diversity. Classification categories may overlap; no uniform transformation campaign is performed.
oracle_or_policy: Keyword/relevance filtering and reference consultation yield a stated 50 articles. Heterogeneous datasets and evaluation objectives explicitly preclude a comparative performance ranking.

counter_history: A cluster may lack a family/version identity; database misses need not mean absence. An upstream vulnerability need not affect downstream execution, and version labels can miss local patches.
inference_limit: Search dates, executable queries and attrition details are unavailable. Internal counts, table descriptions and syntax/semantics terminology conflict. Tool-specific categorical claims require primary-paper checks rather than adoption as universal limitations.

oracle_or_policy: the review or methodological inclusion/evaluation rules reported by the source
claim_ceiling: secondary synthesis of supply-chain security

source_location: Author PDF pp. 1-38: complete retrieved representation; field-specific pages and sections in field_evidence.csv; https://dwermke.com/pdf/journal-tosem-williams25.pdf
evidence_object: Code dependencies, build infrastructure and human participants, together with SBOM/VEX, provenance records and LLM-mediated software development.
observation: A practitioner-informed agenda organizes three attack vectors and cross-cutting directions. It distinguishes transparency from integrity, dependency presence from exploitability, and signing infrastructure from human trust.
transformation_model: Dependency selection, updates, decommissioning, reproducible builds, signing and LLM generation are synthesized from prior work and practitioner perspectives, not a new common-workload transformation experiment.
oracle_or_policy: Eleven 2021-2024 summits report 131 practitioners from 42 companies and 15 US agencies. Authors' research and cited heterogeneous studies supply evidence rather than a systematic-search denominator.
claim_ceiling: Cross-layer research synthesis and agenda, including direct AI-development discussion; not a demonstrated Android assurance architecture, exhaustive census or universally valid security theorem.
counter_history: A present vulnerable dependency may be unused; transparent build records may miss final-artifact injection; signed compromised outputs and self-declared VEX can coexist with insecurity.
inference_limit: Purposeful outreach is not population sampling. Historical framework, regulatory and adoption summaries need their own dates and primary checks. Context-specific tool and model results cannot establish general detection superiority or present-day attack rates.

source_location: Author PDF pp. 1-11: complete retrieved representation; field-specific pages and sections in field_evidence.csv; https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s10207-025-01207-9.pdf
evidence_object: A traditional governance-oriented review of cyber supply-chain methods, principles and standards, mapped to supplier-agnostic foundations and four provider categories.
observation: Academic keyword searches and official-body web searches support a narrative mapping of 30 selected documents. Standards and academic work are separated by supplier type.
transformation_model: Outsourcing, supplier interdependencies, build/update integrity, hardware and cloud responsibilities define the setting. Generative AI appears as deployment risk, not an evaluated generated-code lineage process.
oracle_or_policy: Governance, contracts, executive oversight, certification and shared responsibilities structure treatment recommendations. Commercial-provider methods remain unknown; there is no common calibrated incident or intervention oracle.
claim_ceiling: Secondary coverage of organizational and technical risk treatment, not authenticated artifact ancestry, demonstrated control effectiveness or a cross-layer claim-binding rule.
counter_history: Malicious compromise and defective authorized updates can cause similar downstream disruption but have different histories. Compliance or adoption recommendations do not establish implementation or successful prevention.
inference_limit: The unmeasured web denominator and missing screening attrition constrain completeness. Reported incident totals and regulatory descriptions remain historical secondary claims; no new dataset or controlled effectiveness evaluation is supplied.

source_location: Author PDF pp. 1-27: complete retrieved representation; field-specific pages and sections in field_evidence.csv; https://arxiv.org/pdf/2305.14157
evidence_object: Academic/grey-literature synthesis surveys software-provider/user risks and controls; an existing Atlantic Council dataset supplies selected historical incident trends rather than new observed attacks.
observation: Development/build/distribution stages and transitive dependencies organize vulnerability, integrity, permissions and supplier assessments. Table 2 compiles heterogeneous original-study outcomes, not a common evaluation campaign.
transformation_model: Package/source differences, signing, dependency modification and patch stages are distinct relations. Figure 6 separates commit, release, advisory and client update; complete v1 does not study Android repackaging or AI-generated-code history.
oracle_or_policy: The search reports 290 hits, 222 deduplicated, 22 irrelevant exclusions, 71 after snowballing and 53 eligible studies, without a ledger reconciling transitions. Controls target likelihood, not organization-specific impact.
claim_ceiling: Partial component/version, provenance, authorization, behavioral and claim-limitation antecedents are present. No unified Android artifact-bound cross-layer inference rule is established, and final-2026 equivalence remains unknown.
counter_history: Unused vulnerable components, legitimate maintenance signals and pre-signing corruption defeat simple label-to-verdict inferences. Blanket exclusion of installation-script/inactive projects is a proposed rule, not demonstrated causal prevention.
inference_limit: Version mismatch, unexplained search attrition, repeated references and selected grey-literature incidents limit completeness. No calibrated attack probability, controlled false-rejection study or full lifecycle cost validates proposed controls.

source_location: Author PDF pp. 1-23: complete retrieved representation; field-specific pages and sections in field_evidence.csv; https://arxiv.org/pdf/2304.13261v2
evidence_object: 4,786 SBOM-relevant GitHub discussions from 510 projects supply developer concerns, not 4,786 audited SBOMs. Selection requires an SBOM tag, over ten developers and over 200 issues.
observation: Two authors apply open/axial coding, another confirms categories and disagreements are discussed; a 100-issue pilot supports extraction. Discussion metadata and content yield four lifecycle phases and potential strategies.
transformation_model: Planning, construction/regeneration, secure delivery and maintenance connect inventories to versions, source/artifact links and ownership. AI data/model inventories are discussed, not observations of model-generated code history.
oracle_or_policy: Manual classification and issue opening-to-closing duration operationalize the results. Closed status is not independently verified repair, adoption or accurate SBOM output; categories have unclear overlap/denominators.
claim_ceiling: Evidence supports selected developer-discussion themes and proposed SBOM practices; it cannot establish packaged inclusion, authenticated derivation, license legality, authority or whole-program security.
counter_history: A closed issue can be declined or duplicated; a listed dependency can be missing or misidentified and a suggested tool can fail. Source examples already describe incomplete inventories and failed tooling.
inference_limit: Tag/keyword selection, GitHub-only scope and author coding constrain generalization. Internal status/timing conflicts remain unresolved, final-version equivalence is unknown, and resource anecdotes do not establish lifecycle cost.

source_location: Author PDF pp. 1-13: complete retrieved representation; field-specific pages and sections in field_evidence.csv; https://www.twstalnaker.com/resources/icse24.pdf
evidence_object: Five differentiated stakeholder questionnaires and eight follow-up interviews examine software, AI/data, hardware and operational BOM experiences. Table 3 reports 229 complete, 150 valid and 84 SBOM-familiar responses.
observation: Public-project traces, mailing lists and professional networks recruit respondents. Two annotators independently code using evolving shared labels and reconcile disagreements; eight purposively selected respondents complete consent-recorded interviews.
transformation_model: Source/binary views, build/release/deployment, dependency drift and data/model preprocessing histories are distinguished. Build integration and source-versus-binary consistency are proposals, not implemented cryptographic artifact lineage.
oracle_or_policy: Self-reports and coded themes motivate twelve challenges and four solution directions. C6 separates vulnerable dependency presence from product impact; C7 separates inventory accuracy from transit integrity.
claim_ceiling: Evidence supports selected stakeholder concerns and possible practices, not actual inventory correctness, model-training membership, release authority, legal compliance or measured security improvement.
counter_history: Checksums do not establish inventory completeness; unused vulnerable dependencies need not affect products, and liability requirements can discourage SBOM creation. Proposed solutions explicitly leave interoperability, legacy systems and missing dependencies unresolved.
inference_limit: Self-selection, overlapping roles, variable denominators and tiny specialist groups constrain generalization. Apparent-AI-response exclusion is an author judgment; no current standards/legal certificate or full lifecycle/benefit experiment is established.
